*Early Life*. Raymond III was born circa 1140 to Raymond II Count of Tripoli and his wife Hodierna of Jerusalem. He inherited the county at a young age after his father assassination in 1152. His mother acted as regent until he reached maturity. He grew up amidst the complex politics of the Crusader states and learned the art of diplomacy and warfare.

*Political Career*. After assuming rule Raymond III pursued an active foreign policy. He negotiated treaties with neighboring Muslim leaders and sought to strengthen ties with the Kingdom of Jerusalem. He married Eschiva of Bures thereby gaining claim to the Principality of Galilee and the city of Tiberias. His marriage expanded his influence northward. During the reign of Baldwin IV he served as a key advisor and at times as regent for the young Baldwin V. He attempted to balance the demands of Jerusalem with the needs of his own county. His leadership was marked by both cooperation and conflict with the royal court.

*Later Years and Legacy*. The death of Baldwin V in 1186 triggered a succession crisis. Raymond III supported the claim of Isabella but ultimately Guy of Lusignan secured the crown. Tensions rose and Raymond III withdrew his allegiance. In 1187 he led troops at the Battle of Hattin where the Crusader army suffered a disastrous defeat. Raymond III was captured but later released. He died shortly thereafter in his capital Tripoli in 1187. His passing marked the end of an era of relatively independent Crusader rule in the north. Historians view him as a capable ruler who navigated a treacherous political landscape and left a lasting imprint on the history of the County of Tripoli.
